text:
alexa: Quick heads up Nimbus wants a 3-week pilot to demo live claim extraction into their UI. Requirements: streaming partial parses to the form, function/tool calls to an internal extractor, simple SOC2 answers for procurement, and a ballpark reserved price. Can we draft a dev runbook + pricing blurb?
tom: Stack: Node frontend, Python workers, small Go ingress. Confirmed.
ravi: Ill assemble a minimal Python SDK example that shows SSE + function_call resume flow. Tiny snippet:```py
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
stream = client.stream(model="redwood-medium", stream=True, structured_output=True, tools=[{"name":"claim_extractor"}])
for event in stream.events():
    if event.type=="function_call":
        res = call_internal_extractor(event.args['text'])
        stream.resume(tool_result=res)
    elif event.type=="response":
        print(event.partial_json)
```
Use small timeouts on extractor calls to avoid blocking the stream.
marie: Ops note: For a short pilot use batch_size=1, max_concurrency=3, prefix_kv_cache=true if you're reusing policy docs. Use the quantized runtime if 100-200ms gain is worth a slight quality delta. Set fallback policy to a cheaper variant to avoid hard failures.
sasha: Security checklist for procurement: 1) data residency (which regions?), 2) retention window (are >30d logs required?), 3) KMS/CMEK requirements, 4) subprocessors. If they will send PHI/PII propose Redwood Private (VPC) for the pilot. I can prefill the form if we get their security contact + one sample payload.
alexa: Pricing sketch? We need an upfront reserved bucket for 3 weeks and overage rules.
marie: Suggest: small reserved capacity for pilot (baseline 1-2 qps sustained) ~ $5k-$7k for 3 weeks depending on model size + usage overage at list. Offer a one-time POC discount (15-25%) subject to deal desk approval. Audit/log retention add-on priced separately.
tom: SSE question: can we stream intermediate function_call events to the browser?
ravi: Yes. SSE streams will emit function_call and subsequent tool_result events. For true bidirectional low-latency (adapter influences generation mid-token) websockets are preferable, but a common pattern: emit function_call via SSE -> adapter responds -> call /streams/resume with tool_result. That keeps UI realtime enough for form population.
marie: Quick runbook fragment (copyable):```yaml
POC_RUNBOOK:
  env:
    - REDWOOD_API_KEY set
    - REGION=us-west-2
  start_stream:
    - curl -N "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-medium" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -d '{"input":"...","structured_output":true}'
  on_function_call:
    - POST /internal/extract -> adapter returns JSON -> POST /streams/resume {"tool_result": <json>}
  runtime_defaults:
    - batch_size: 1
    - max_concurrency: 3
    - prefix_kv_cache: true
    - fallback: smaller-model
  observability:
    - include X-TRACE header in requests
    - set log level=warn for POC
```
sasha: For the SOC2 packet Ill draft answers for standard procurement Qs. Need the customer's security contact email + an example claim payload (headers ok, redact PII).
alexa: Actions: Ravi -> Python example + short Node demo; Marie -> ops defaults + single-page pricing blurb; Sasha -> prefilled security pack; Tom -> coordinate with Nimbus and get security contact. Aim to ship customer-ready package within 24 hours. :thumbsup:
redwood-bot: Reminder: tag with #poc-handovers when assets are uploaded so sales-ops can pick up onboarding steps.
alexa: Thanks team, will consolidate and DM the Nimbus contact once we have the bundle.
